entries.title: II Corinthians 8:2
segments: The riches of their liberality. The Gentile churches of Macedonia, though themselves in deep poverty, had sent a contribution to the poor Jewish Christians at Jerusalem.  See
.  The Macedonian churches mentioned in the New Testament are those of Philippi, Thessalonica and Beroea.

entries.title: II Corinthians 8:6
segments: This grace also. It would appear that the Corinthians were lacking in ordinary generosity.  When Paul was preaching among them he was supported by funds contributed by other churches, the church at Philippi being his dependence.  See
. The churches in Macedonia had given of their own accord (
): the Corinthians had to be asked for their contribution by Titus.

entries.title: II Corinthians 8:18
segments: The brother whose praise... is spread through all the churches. No clue is given as to the identity of this brother.  Some commentators surmise that he was Luke; others, Tychicus, so often Paul's faithful messenger.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 8:22
segments: Our brother. Also unknown. The two who accompanied Titus to gather the collection were probably delegated by the contributing churches at Paul's request (
).  One may have been Epaphroditus, the messenger of the church at Philippi to Paul at Rome.  See

entries.title: II Corinthians 8:24
segments: Our glorying on your behalf. See
